Complexity: $O(1+L\Delta\varepsilon^{-2}[1+(\sigma/\varepsilon)^{p/(p-1)}])$ stochastic-gradient calls, including minibatches, for $\mathbb E\|\nabla f(X)\|\le\varepsilon$ using tuned minibatch normalized SGD.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Lower-bounded differentiable objectives with globally L-Lipschitz gradients; convexity is not required. The initial gap to a lower bound is at most Δ, with L,Δ>0.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: One unbiased gradient sample g(x,ω) per call, with i.i.d. seeds; only gradient samples are supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ParameterFreeHeavyTailedSmooth.lean: spec.admissible, oracle answer and unbiasedness clauses; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID

distinctive_assumptions.label: unknown_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: Only the real separable Hilbert space E and initial point x0 are public. L,Δ,σ,p,ε are hidden from the algorithm constructor; execution is truncated at the supplied parameter-dependent budget.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform central moment bound E‖g(x,ω)−∇f(x)‖^p≤σ^p for 1<p≤2 and σ≥0; finite variance is not required when p<2.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is a complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure and second-countable topology; finite dimension is not assumed.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: A measurable E-valued output X must have integrable gradient norm and satisfy E‖∇f(X)‖≤ε, with ε>0.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over independent algorithm randomness and the i.i.d. oracle stream, under a fixed parameter-dependent cap on oracle calls.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth lower-bounded nonconvex optimization with unbiased i.i.d. gradients having a bounded central p-th moment is an established heavy-tailed stochastic optimization formulation, including study of unknown problem parameters.
